title: Exchanging the order of integration for the failure probability
statement:
Let $X \times Y$ be a finite set equipped with a probability measure $\mu$, let $p$ be a one-way public-coin protocol with inputs in $X$ and $Y$, outputs in $\alpha$, and shared randomness ranging over coin tapes of length $m$, and let $f : X \times Y \to \alpha$ be a target function. Write $\mathrm{rrun}(p, x, y, \omega)$ for the output produced by running $p$ on inputs $x$ and $y$ under coin tape $\omega$, and let $\nu$ be the measure carried by the coin tapes of length $m$. Then
\[
  \int \mu\bigl(\{(x,y) : \mathrm{rrun}(p,x,y,\omega) \neq f(x,y)\}\bigr)\,d\nu(\omega)
  \;=\;
  \int \nu\bigl(\{\omega : \mathrm{rrun}(p,x,y,\omega) \neq f(x,y)\}\bigr)\,d\mu(x,y),
\]
where each measure is read as a real number. That is, integrating the $\mu$-probability of failure over the choice of coin tape yields the same value as integrating the $\nu$-probability of failure over the choice of input pair.
hypotheses_covered: X × Y is a finite probability space with measure μ
p is a one-way public-coin protocol over coin tapes of length m, inputs X and Y, output α
f : X × Y → α is a target function
coin tapes of length m carry their measure ν (volume)
each set measure is taken as a real number (toReal)
replaced:
Let $\mu$ be a finite probability measure on $X \times Y$, let $p$ be a one-way
public-coin protocol with coin tape of length $m$, and let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$.
Then
\[
  \int_{\omega}\Pr_{(x,y)\sim\mu}\bigl[p.\mathrm{rrun}(x,y,\omega)\neq f(x,y)\bigr]\,d\omega
  \;=\;
  \int_{(x,y)\sim\mu}\Pr_{\omega}\bigl[p.\mathrm{rrun}(x,y,\omega)\neq f(x,y)\bigr]\,d\mu,
\]
i.e.\ the order of integration over the coin tape and the input distribution may be
exchanged (Fubini's theorem applied to the $\{0,1\}$-valued failure indicator).
